alerts.title: Coastal flooding statement
alerts.summary: In effect for Coastline from Farrant Island to Price Island.
alerts.officialText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by strong winds and large waves are expected this week.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides.

When:
During high tides today.

Additional information:
A low pressure system will cross Haida Gwaii today bringing strong winds, storm surge and large waves. This will coincide with a run of king tides, elevating water levels 20 to 50 cm higher than the highest astronomical tides.  

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

alerts.title: Snowfall warning
alerts.summary: In effect for Highway 3 - Paulson Summit to Kootenay Pass.
alerts.officialText:
Snow, heavy at times, is expected.

Where: Highway 3 - Paulson Summit to Kootenay Pass.

When: Today and tonight.

What: 15 to 25 cm of snow.

Remarks: A moisture-laden system has pushed into southern B.C. overnight. Heavy snow will ease early this afternoon. However, light to moderate snow is expected to continue through tonight. Strong southerly winds will accompany the heavy snow, occasionally reducing visibility significantly.

Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

Weather in the mountains can change suddenly resulting in hazardous driving conditions.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Allow extra time for travel. The site https://shiftintowinter.ca/ reminds drivers to know before you go. Adjust to winter driving behaviour and use winter tires and chains.

Road conditions are available at https://www.drivebc.ca/.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

alerts.title: Coastal flooding warning
alerts.summary: In effect for Coastline from Harbledown Island to Hardwicke Island incl. Knight Inlet.
alerts.officialText:
This warning is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Moderate flooding along coastlines and low-lying areas due to storm surge, large waves and high tides.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides.

When:
During high tides today.

Additional information:
A strong frontal system will track across the B.C. coast tonight and Thursday, bringing storm surge and large waves. This will coincide with king tides, elevating water levels 30 to 60 cm higher than astronomical tides to produce moderate to significant coastal flooding.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Unsafe driving conditions due to flooded roads and/or debris, such as driftwood and rocks, is possible. Coastal erosion is likely in sensitive areas, such as tidal flats, estuaries, dunes, beaches or barrier islands. Ground floors of some properties and parts of communities may be affected by flooding.

Residents should take immediate action to protect life and property. Heed advice from emergency management organizations. Prepare your property by moving valuables and harmful chemicals from your basement or crawl space to safe, elevated locations. Secure loose objects that may be carried away by water. Stay away from the shore to prevent being swept off rocks, injured by heavy objects such as rocks or driftwood or pulled out to sea.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
